summary.headline: Geojit's FY26 profit absorbed planned investments; distribution income up 10% and equity MF net inflow share rose to 0.40 from 0.33.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as the first year of "Geojit 2.0", a shift toward recurring income (mutual fund distribution, advisory, PMS, insurance) with investments in sales headcount, IT and brand. Net sales headcount rose by about 700 to 3,768, including 650 in sales, at a cost of about INR29 crores, and brand spend rose by about INR15 crores. Profitability was hit by these investments, with about INR54 crores of transformation expenses booked and ROE reduced as brokerage income fell. Management said the next two years would carry similar investment costs, and it stopped field hiring for the current year because of the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.metric: Equity MF net inflow market share
Transformation / investment expenses booked in FY26

financial_highlights.change: total cash about INR1,115 crores, of which INR700-800 crores already deployed in MTF and lending
PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY; INR450 crores in FY23
NRI income about INR90 crores in FY26

segments.name: Broking and distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution income grew 10% in FY26 while brokerage income declined, which management cited as the reason for lower ROE. Legacy clients (7+ years) contribute 58-60% of broking and MF income.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Equity MF net inflow market share improved to 0.40 from 0.33 while industry equity net inflows were down about 20%. MF AUM per client rose to about INR5 lakh from about INR3.5 lakh in FY22.

segments.name: Insurance distribution
segments.commentary: Health insurance premium of close to INR22 crores in its first year of distribution, previously life only.

segments.name: Private Wealth
segments.commentary: AUM about INR2,400 crores; about 55 RMs and 90 staff; plans to hire 25-30 RMs in FY27; around 5 to 8 branch cities with no new cities planned.

segments.name: DIFC / Middle East
segments.commentary: DIFC entity licensed and operational since February 2026 as an external asset manager to private banks; 3 staff and client onboarding expected to start by end of May 2026. Minimum ticket size about USD 1 million.

segments.name: PMS / AIF
segments.commentary: PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY; one AIF via GIFT City in application stage; 1-2 more PMS schemes expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No field hiring for the current year given the West Asia conflict; vacancies to be backfilled and training of FY26 hires prioritised.
IT transformation: about INR30 crores over the next three years, focused on digital, data and client-facing systems.
Transformation investments in people and IT expected at similar levels for the next two years; funded from internal resources, with no plan to raise capital.
New salespeople expected to break even in 12-18 months, faster when broking is involved and slower for MF-only sales.
Management will borrow externally to fund future MTF, LAS and NBFC lending growth rather than using own cash.
Buyback to be considered once SEBI regulations are finalised; no forward ROE or growth figures given.
capex_capacity: Sales headcount: about 700 net additions in FY26 (650 in sales), total employees 3,768; field hiring paused for the current year.
IT transformation phase 1 spend about INR10 crores in FY26; about INR30 crores planned over the next three years.
Private Wealth: 25-30 RM hires planned in FY27 on top of about 55 RMs.
DIFC: 3 staff currently, with RM recruitment in progress.
Liquid cash about INR375 crores, with the balance of about INR1,115 crores deployed in MTF, LAS and NBFC lending.
demand_pricing: Equity MF net inflow share improved to 0.40 from 0.33 while industry equity MF net inflows were down about 20%.
SIP monthly collection reached INR151 crores in March 2026.
Management said April 2026 was too early to call; clients are deferring financial decisions until West Asia clarity emerges, but no panic redemptions were seen in the NRI base.
Management expects the domestic MF industry to grow at least double digits over 2-5 years.
Insurance (including health) is being used as a substitute for market-linked products when equity markets are weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is the DIFC entity traction, and how does it differ from the existing Middle East JVs? What is the NRI AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: DIFC is a private banking external-asset-manager business that started operations in February 2026, with client onboarding expected by end-May 2026. Existing Middle East entities are retail-focused. NRI AUM is INR12,000-13,000 crores, with about INR90 crores of income in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring and capex plans for the current year?
qa_highlights.answer: Field hiring has been stopped because of the West Asia crisis; only replacements will be made. IT spend of about INR30 crores is planned over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback plans and borrowing to fund MTF, given cash of about INR1,100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that borrowing is cheaper than using own cash and said it intends to borrow for MTF, LAS and NBFC needs. Buyback will be considered after SEBI rules are issued.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic client reaction in March and April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clients increased investments in MF, and that April was too early to judge given the ceasefire uncertainty. Management expects short-term apprehension but long-term industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: ROE trajectory and dilution from the strategic shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward ROE guidance. It said ROE fell because brokerage declined while distribution income rose; no equity raise is planned and the transformation will be funded internally.

qa_highlights.question: PMS growth is modest. What are the bottlenecks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY to INR1,450 crores and that the team has been selling PMS for only three years.

risks_watch: Profitability pressure from about two more years of investment costs, with ROE already lower because brokerage income fell.
West Asia conflict: clients are deferring decisions and DIFC onboarding may slow; monitor April-June inflows and DIFC client wins.
Sales productivity of the roughly 650 new sales hires against the 12-18 month break-in target.
Funding of MTF and lending growth via borrowings, given the cost and capital effects of moving from cash-funded to debt-funded lending.
Pending SEBI buyback framework and any capital allocation decision.
summary.management_tone: Confident on distribution traction and MF market share gains, but cautious on near-term hiring, the West Asia impact and April business. Management declined to give forward ROE or growth numbers and deferred buyback decisions to SEBI rules.
key_quotes: For most brokers, a transaction is the end. For Geojit, a transaction is just the beginning, the starting point of a long-term wealth relationship.
Our net inflow market share in equities for mutual fund improved from 0.33 to 0.40 reflecting an improving competitiveness and deeper client engagement.
So, at the moment, we have stopped recruiting.
We are not looking at raising capital as of now. There is nothing on the line nor discussion also.
